name: Gilded-Rime
geological_features: Frozen ammonia seas with golden crystalline surface
Ice cliffs hundreds of meters tall with metallic inclusions
Petrified remnants of former biosphere frozen in the ice
specific_features: Ancient alien ruins embedded in the ice sheet
description: Gilded-Rime is named for the extraordinary appearance of its frozen ammonia seas, whose surfaces have crystallized into a golden lattice that catches any available light and multiplies it into a warm glow that contradicts the world's bitter cold. The ice cliffs that border these seas are streaked with metallic inclusions that gleam in bands of gold and silver, and the petrified remains of an ancient biosphere can be seen embedded in the ice like insects in amber, frozen mid-motion in postures of life.

The golden light reflecting off the ammonia seas creates an illusion of warmth that is immediately and cruelly dispelled by the actual temperature. The thin atmosphere carries ice crystals that refract the golden light into halos and rings, making the world appear gilded even in its harshest conditions. The silence is profound, broken only by the sharp crack of ice expanding and contracting in the temperature swings between day and night, sounds that carry for kilometers in the cold, still air.

The petrified biosphere tells the story of a world that was once warm enough to support complex life, with visible fossils of organisms that bear no resemblance to any known xenobiological taxonomy. Alien ruins embedded in the ice suggest that intelligent beings once inhabited this world, and the ruins' positioning correlates with the densest fossil beds, implying a relationship between the civilization and the native life. The transition from living world to frozen wasteland was apparently rapid, as the fossils show no signs of the slow decline that typically precedes an ice age.

The dark crystal deposits found near the alien ruins are of a type associated with advanced energy manipulation technology, and their presence suggests the previous civilization may have been responsible for their own world's destruction through a catastrophic energy experiment. The platinum deposits in the ice cliffs are accessible and valuable, but the archaeological significance of the frozen biosphere has prevented large-scale extraction. The ruins remain partially buried, and each centimeter of ice removed reveals new questions about what happened here and whether the same fate could befall other worlds.
